items.q: What does the Instant Gratification Monkey care about?
items.a: **Easy and fun. Now.** No memory of the past, no knowledge of the future. Fine for a dog. Lost in a civilization that needs unfun work for a later payoff. Wikipedia of Kerrigan/Harding, fridge check, Feynman magnets → Justin Bieber's mom.

items.q: What is the only thing that scares the monkey off the wheel?
items.a: The **Panic Monster** — dormant until a deadline, public embarrassment, or career disaster gets close. TED booked Urban six months out; he Google-Earthed India. The **speaker page with his face** woke the monster. Then he could write the talk.

items.q: Why isn't Dark Playground fun actually fun?
items.a: Leisure **at the wrong time** — entirely outside the 'makes sense' circle. Unearned. The air is **guilt, dread, anxiety, self-hatred**. Dinner and sleep after work are the same activities in the overlap zone.

items.q: Why does Urban say the funny kind of procrastination is not the dangerous one?
items.a: Deadline delay is **contained** — the monster eventually ships the paper (90 pages / 72 hours / very bad). **No due date** on art, a company, family, health, leaving a bad relationship. Effects extend outward forever. Emails: spectators in their own lives, never even started the chase.

items.q: What is the Life Calendar, and what job does it assign?
items.a: One box per week of a **90-year** life. Not that many, and some are used. Stay aware of the monkey — especially where there is **no deadline**. Start today. The monkey's closer: well, maybe not today. Sometime soon.
